**What this PR does / why we need it**:
When using Azure Standard Load Balancer backed K8S cluster, previously K8S cloud provider will not set the EnableTCPReset to true in new load balancer rules added to a Standard Load Balancer. This change fixes the issue and always set the value to true as that's one of the benefits of Azure Standard Load Blancer over Basic Load Balancer.
**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

issue_context.title: K8S Azure Cloud Provider doesn't not set enableTcpReset to true in load balancer rules for Azure Standard Load Blancer
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
1. Create a k8s cluster backed by Azure Standard Load Balancer
2. Create a LoadBalancer type service and wait till the service is up
3. Go to Azure portal and examine the Azure Standard Load Balancer

The load balancer rule added by k8s cloud provider for the new service doesn't have a "true" value in enableTcpReset property

**What you expected to happen**:
A "true" value in the enableTcpReset property of the load balancer rule is expected.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
See above.
**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.13.7
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Azure
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments:
As per Azure documentation on this feature (https://docs.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/load-balancer/load-balancer-tcp-reset), this is only a preview feature and not recommended for production workloads. Is the ask to to enable this by default for all K8s deployments in Azure?

![Screen Shot 2019-07-22 at 5 20 32 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1331160/61673616-0da4db80-aca5-11e9-87d8-5fb6579626f3.png)

Agreed with @Koderok. I think we should enable this feature by an annotation, and only enable it when the service has set the annotation. e.g. `service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-load-balancer-enable-tcp-reset=true`

updated the PR with service annotation as suggested - but confirmed from PM that this feature in network is technically GA, the only reason that it is not publicly announced is because the Azure portal change is not ready, based on this - do you think we will need to remove this annotation one day? if so, should we do it now? @feiskyer @Koderok

review_comments: Return error when basic load balancer is used here. Failing silently without errors would confuse users.
